newsitem.title: UK: Siebe falls on negative APV deal sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Siebe falls on negative APV deal sentiment.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc dropped on Monday amid negative comment on the company's 327.4 million stg acquisition of process engineering group APV Plc, dealers said.
NatWest repeated a "reduce" stance on the stock, market sources said, and some weekend press comment was doubtful on the benefits of the deal.
There was also talk that Germany's GEA could make a counter bid for APV, whose shares were down 1p at 105-1/2, though GEA made no reference to APV in its results statement on Monday.

Siebe shares were down 8p at 962 by 1217 GMT in volume of 1.4 million shares, after earlier dropping as low as 955p -- for the time being capping a rebound from the eight-month low of 889p set on April 29.
Saturday's Lex column in the Financial Times said Siebe was taking on "considerable risk" with the acquisition and that its target of boosting APV's margins to ten percent "looks challenging."
NatWest analysts were not immediately available for comment.

Meanwhile, Siebe chief executive Allen Yurko repeated his confidence in the deal in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. Yurko said it was a "critical" move for Siebe, creating a global presence in the process engineering industry.

He denied that the price Siebe had paid was too high. "The price is on the low side, when you consider all the things that Siebe will gain and when you consider all the value it will give to Siebe shareholders," Yurko said.
Siebe said on Friday the acquisition would be earnings-enhancing from the outset.

Separately analysts at BZW repeated a "buy" recommendation on Siebe shares, arguing that the acquisition gave the company an opportunity to extend sales of high margin Foxboro control systems into the food, beverage and drug markets, dealers said.
Analysts at BZW were not immediately available for comment.
Siebe's financial adviser, Morgan Stanley, is to dispatch the formal offer to APV shareholders by May 24.
